name: Champagne
hook: The French sparkling wine with its own monk, glass, bottle sizes and cocktail canon.

facts.label: Dom Pérignon
facts.statement: Dom Pérignon was a 17th-century monk and cellar master at the Abbey of Hautvillers; Moët & Chandon introduced the champagne brand named for him in 1936.

facts.label: brut
facts.statement: Brut is the term for a dry champagne; "extra brut" means even drier.

facts.label: the flute
facts.statement: Champagne is served in a flute, a tall stemmed glass that shares its name with a musical instrument and a column groove.

facts.label: a magnum
facts.statement: A magnum holds 1.5 liters of champagne — twice the standard bottle.

facts.label: French 75
facts.statement: The French 75 is champagne and gin, named for the 75mm field gun of World War I.

facts.label: mimosa
facts.statement: A mimosa is champagne mixed with orange juice, often served at brunch.

facts.label: Cole Porter
facts.statement: Cole Porter wrote "I Get a Kick Out of You," with its line "I get no kick from champagne."
associations: I Get a Kick Out of You
